provenance.case: Grameen Bank group lending and joint liability (1976 onward; Grameen II around 2002)

target.task: Our university electronics lab lends 40 portable kits (oscilloscope, multimeter, Arduino board) to 120 second-year students for take-home practice. Last term, damaged or missing parts cost the lab 85,000 BDT, and nobody felt responsible. Design a borrowing scheme.

rules.text: Borrowers may be organised in groups of 2 to 6 students, or a group size of 1 for no groups.
Who pays for damage must be one of: group, individual, lab.
Any deposit is from 0 to 500 BDT per student.
Give 2 to 5 rules, open to every second-year student whatever their gender.

target.format: Reply with JSON only, in this shape: {"group_size": 1, "who_pays_for_damage": "group, individual or lab", "deposit_bdt_per_student": 0, "rules": ["..."]}

source_example.text: Grameen Bank grew out of an experiment that the economist Muhammad Yunus began in 1976 in Jobra, a village next to Chittagong University. His first loans, about 27 US dollars in total, went to 42 women, among them makers of bamboo stools. Ordinary banks would not lend to such borrowers because they had no collateral. Grameen's answer was the group: a borrower joined a group of five people who lived nearby and chose each other. Loans went first to two members, then to two more, and last to the group chair, each step depending on the earlier borrowers repaying. Group members were jointly responsible, so a member who did not repay hurt the chances of the others. Because of this, members chose partners they trusted, checked on each other and helped one another through bad weeks. Groups met weekly with a bank worker at a centre in the village and repaid in small weekly instalments. Most borrowers were women, and Grameen reported repayment rates above 95 percent. In 2006 Yunus and Grameen Bank shared the Nobel Peace Prize. Around 2002 Grameen replaced the strict joint-liability rules with a more flexible system often called Grameen II. Economists still debate how much of the high repayment came from joint liability itself and how much from weekly meetings and careful staff.

incidental_details.text: First loans of 27 dollars to 42 women

relation: Peer groups that share responsibility make members choose and support each other.
